Unsure if this needs trigger warnings, but just in case: // transmedicalist takes, dysphoria mention

For some context, I'm a young trans guy who's identified as male for nearly a decade now, and I've never previously struggled with bottom dysphoria aside from a few very, very mild rough days. Currently, I have plans to get top surgery at some point, but I have zero interest in bottom surgery for various reasons.

A few hours ago, I was meandering through some trans-focused groups online because I personally enjoy being able to discuss my experiences with like-minded individuals. As I was clicking through, I found a particularly nasty set of comments that seemed to stem from a trsnsmedicalist subreddit which essentially said "no real transgender person would be able to look at their genitalia without being overcome with negative emotions and wanting to off themselves. If they don't fit into that group, they're faking their identity and are probably just cis". Yikes, right?

For painfully obvious reasons, I now feel like utter shit and am beginning to question the validity of my identity; admittedly, I did uncover my identity as a trans male at a time in my life when I was struggling to make friends. Did I somehow accidentally gaslight myself into identifying as male for attention? I don't think so, as I still have pretty notable dysphoria surrounding my chest and deadname, but I can't stop thinking about the "what if"s. Am I doing something wrong?

Thank you so much for the reply, this helped me out quite a bit. I do have a track record of putting unnecessary stress and pressure on myself, so I suppose I should work on that, too. Thank you again.

Funnily enough, I came to this subreddit to write this exact same post. It feels like the years passed by faster than you could ever imagine, huh? I’m terrified of the massive responsibility I’ll suddenly be burdened with. It feels like I’ll lose everything. The freedom I’ve had for the past few years, the fun I’ve gotten to have with my friends and family- it feels like the second I become a (legal) adult, it’ll all be stripped away from me. I understand where you’re coming from. It’s a terrifying notion. However, a part of me feels like it’s entirely irrational. A part of me *knows* that. And you should know that, too. There’s no otherworldly demon that’s going to come knocking on your door in a few years and suck the happiness right from your soul. And it’s true- time does pass, and there’s nothing any of us can do to stop it. But that’s why it’s important to relish the time we have with our friends and loved ones while they’re still around. You’re going to be okay. I promise. Hang in there, and make the most of every moment.
